headline: Recursive releases Flint: 39.8B-parameter open coding model, 2.5B active
quote: The Recursive Flint local coding model is a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 40B total and 2.5B active parameters.
claim: Recursive released Flint, its first model, with weights on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0; MarkTechPost's 21 Oct 2026 report lists 39.8B total and about 2.5B active parameters and a documented context of 262,144 tokens. It says 4-bit weights take about 23 GB (INT4 MLX 22.6 GB, NVFP4 GGUF 22.9 GB) with Recursive recommending a 48 GB Mac or GPU, and gives self-reported scores of 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified and 54.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1.
why_it_matters: An open Apache 2.0 coding model you can run yourself: about 23 GB of 4-bit weights, but Recursive recommends 48 GB of memory, so check your laptop first.
title: Recursive Releases Flint, an Open-Weight 40B MoE Local Coding Model for Agents with 2.5B Active Params - MarkTechPost

headline: llama.cpp adds DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash support in build b11870
claim: llama.cpp build b11870 (25 Oct, listed as a Pre-release on GitHub) merges pull request #31086, "model: DSV4.1 flash", which adds DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (deepseek41) to the runtime. Its commit notes include converting the Engram table to BF16 and gathering Engram rows in-graph.
why_it_matters: Mainline llama.cpp now has a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash implementation, but Unsloth's smallest quant of the model is 233.0 GB, so it is a workstation model, not a laptop one.
verify_note: published date has no evidence text found in the page (set published_evidence to a verbatim snippet)
title: Release b11870 · ggml-org/llama.cpp · GitHub

headline: Unsloth lists DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash quants from 233.0 GB to 508.4 GB
quote: Our 250.4 GB 1-bit UD-IQ1_M quant achieves 88.2% top-1 agreement against original DeepSeek and runs locally on 128GB+ RAM setups.
claim: Unsloth's run-locally guide for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (page last updated 19 Oct 2026) lists GGUF quants from 233.0 GB (UD-IQ1_S) to 508.4 GB (UD-Q8_K_XL) and puts memory needs at 128–145 GB for 1-bit up to 315 GB for 8-bit. Its 250.4 GB UD-IQ1_M quant is reported at 88.2% top-1 agreement with DeepSeek's original on the long17k test.
why_it_matters: A reality check: even the 1-bit quant wants 128 GB or more of memory, so on a student laptop this model stays an API option.
title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Run Locally Guide | Unsloth Documentationx-twitterlinkedindiscordblueskyreddit

headline: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: E4B needs roughly 6GB RAM, 74B-A9B 24-32GB
quote: E4B runs on roughly 4GB VRAM or 6GB RAM.
claim: Unsloth's run-locally guide (page last updated 23 Oct 2026) describes NVIDIA's open Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B (8B parameters, 4B effective, 64K context) and Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B (74B total, 9B active, 128K context). It lists E4B Q4_K_M as a 6.18GB download needing roughly 4GB VRAM or 6GB RAM, and the 22GB IQ2_XXS quant of 74B-A9B as needing 24–32GB RAM; the page does not state a licence.
why_it_matters: Stated memory figures for a small and a mid-size model: about 6GB RAM for E4B, 24-32GB for the 74B-A9B quant. Check them against your own laptop's RAM.
title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: Run Locally Guide | Unsloth Documentationx-twitterlinkedindiscordblueskyreddit

headline: IBM releases Granite Speech 5.0 2B, Apache 2.0 speech model
quote: Granite Speech 5.0 2B is a compact and efficient speech-language model, specifically designed for multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR)
claim: IBM's Granite Speech 5.0 2B (2B parameters, BF16 safetensors) is an Apache 2.0 model for speech recognition and speech translation in English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Japanese, with a stated release date of 20 Oct 2026. It was trained on 390,000 hours of audio, and the card has usage sections for transformers, vLLM, llama.cpp and mlx-audio for Apple Silicon.
why_it_matters: A 2B Apache 2.0 speech-to-text and translation model with llama.cpp and Apple MLX usage notes; its listed languages include no Indian ones, so Hindi voice projects need another model.
title: ibm-granite/granite-speech-5.0-2b · Hugging Face

headline: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Embed, Rerank and Parse retrieval models
quote: Today, we are expanding the Nemotron Retriever collection with new open, commercially available models for embedding, reranking, and document extraction.
claim: NVIDIA's team published on 21 Oct 2026 Nemotron 3.5 Embed (8B BF16, 1B BF16, 1B NVFP4), Rerank (8B BF16) and Parse (631M parameters), which it calls open, commercially available models. It reports Embed 8B BF16 at 61.17 nDCG@10 on ViDoRe v3.1, first among dense retrieval models as of 10/20/2026, with the distilled 1B BF16 at 58.38, or 95.4% of the 8B score.
why_it_matters: Open embedding, reranking and document-parsing models for RAG projects, including a 1B embedder and a 631M parser; check the model-card licence before building on them.
title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed, Rerank, and Parse: Advancing Agents with World-Class Retrieval Models

headline: Hugging Face ships AnyLanguageModel 1.0 for local models on Apple platforms
quote: AnyLanguageModel 1.0 is out, along with swift-huggingface 1.0 and swift-xet 1.0.
claim: Hugging Face released AnyLanguageModel 1.0 on 20 Oct 2026, a Swift package that lets apps use Apple's Foundation Models API with open-weight models through llama.cpp, MLX and Core ML as well as hosted providers. The post lists Gemma 4 E2B GGUF at about 3.4 GB (Q4_0), LFM2.5 2.6B GGUF at about 1.7 GB (Q4_K_M) and Qwen3.8 27B for MLX at about 16 GB at 4 bits, and says Qwen3.8 27B runs on a Mac with 32 GB of memory or more.
why_it_matters: If you build for iPhone or Mac, one Swift API now covers local and hosted models; the post says small open models are a good place to start.
title: AnyLanguageModel 1.0: One Year of Local Models on Apple Platforms
